chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabalah from a number of the companions of Ali, and I do not know Sulayman except that he informed me of it, and Ali ibn Abdullah from Sulayman also from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) that he said:
"Bind them to what they bound themselves to."
ai.seo_question: What is the legal principle regarding binding individuals to their own commitments in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of Chapter 29 regarding the inheritance of siblings, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *al-lazm* (binding obligation), where parties are held to the specific terms they voluntarily accepted. This maxim is widely cited by Shia jurists to validate contractual stipulations in inheritance distribution, ensuring that voluntary agreements override default statutory shares when explicitly agreed upon.
